legend: An array c$$$c$$$ of length n$$$n$$$ is good if it satisfies the following property:
For all 1<i≤n$$$1  \lt  i \le n$$$, there exists some j<i$$$j  \lt  i$$$ such that gcd(ci,cj)>1$$$\gcd(c_i, c_j)  \gt  1$$$.

We can measure the cost of some array b$$$b$$$ of n$$$n$$$ integers. In one operation, you can remove any good subsequence from the array. The cost of b$$$b$$$ is the minimum number of operations to make the array empty.
You're given an array a$$$a$$$ of length n$$$n$$$. You want to minimise the cost of a$$$a$$$ by performing the following action exactly once:
Choose positions l$$$l$$$ and r$$$r$$$ such that 1≤l≤r≤n$$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$.
Perform a cyclic shift to the right on the subarray al…r$$$a_{l \ldots r}$$$.
Please output the minimum cost after performing the following action exactly once on a$$$a$$$.
input: Each test consists of several test cases. The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤103$$$1 \le t \le 10^3$$$) — the number of test cases. This is followed by descriptions of the test cases.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤3⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the size of the array a$$$a$$$.
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤3⋅105$$$1 \le a_i \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$).
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 3⋅105$$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum cost of a$$$a$$$ after performing the given action exactly once.
note: In the first sample, one optimal selection is to perform the action with l=2$$$l = 2$$$ and r=5$$$r = 5$$$. After performing the action, a=[10,6,9,8,7,5,4,3,2,1]$$$a = [10, 6, 9, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]$$$. We can show that the cost of this a$$$a$$$ is equal to 3$$$3$$$:

In the second operation, remove the subsequence [7]$$$[7]$$$.
In the third operation, remove the subsequence [1]$$$[1]$$$.
